spec_match.rationale: Runs the exact shipping pipeline (MSE addSourceBuffer/appendBuffer with the spec-form string iamf.000.000.Opus muxed with avc1.640028) against the same asset Chromium's MSE_BasicPlayback_Iamf_Stereo integration test plays.

interactive.rationale: One button drives the six-rung ladder with per-rung live outcomes, a visible video element with controls, and a real downloadable asset.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index card promises a real playback attempt that stops honestly where the browser stops; the verified behaviour is exactly a rung-1 stop on the test browser.

edge_cases.rationale: No-MediaSource, probe-false, fetch failure, addSourceBuffer throw, autoplay rejection, and decode-after-positive-probe divergence all have distinct honest branches — but rungs 2-6 could not be executed in any available browser, so those branches remain code-reviewed and syntax-loaded rather than runtime-proven.

references.rationale: Links ChromeStatus, the spec's ISO-BMFF encapsulation section, and the upstream crsrc asset with license attribution — plus an explicit pointer that the served file is the v152 copy, shared rather than duplicated.

conformance.rationale: The v153 feature suite pins the probe contracts the ladder depends on (resolve-not-reject, MSE-door agreement, malformed refusal); 9/9 pass in the verification browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP page-driver run (headless Chromium 141): rung 1 renders both isTypeSupported answers (false/false) and the ladder stops with the honest blocked explanation naming the anticipated-153 flip, rungs 2-6 stay 'not run yet', console/network clean (no fetch issued on the blocked path); the shared v152 asset URL separately verified 200 video/mp4 117384 bytes; screenshot v153-iamf-player.png read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Success asserts iamf-mse-playback with duration/currentTime; every stop rung asserts iamf-mse-blocked with the rung and reason; autoplay-block asserts its own id.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; rung badges use the darkened-emerald/rose/muted trio on ivory (AA); button follows the global dark pattern.

accessibility.rationale: The ladder is a labelled list with textual per-rung state (badge glyphs are backed by adjacent text), the video has controls and an aria-label, and the outcome line is role=status aria-live=polite.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Inherits the v152 overflow-wrap fix on rung titles; responsive-check passes both classes with no horizontal overflow; screenshots judged clean.

openQuestions.title: Execute rungs 2-6 on an IAMF-enabled Chromium
openQuestions.detail: The success path (fetch, append, endOfStream, play with advancing currentTime) has never run in a real browser here because no available build decodes IAMF. When a Chrome 153 build with the flip landed (or an iamf-tools build with --enable-features=IamfAudioDecoding) is available, run the full ladder against the shared v152 asset URL, confirm currentTime advances and the iamf-mse-playback assert passes, and update this critique's edge_cases to pass.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Expose stepwise async progress as text, keep native media controls, and never communicate state by colour or icon alone.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each rung has a text outcome beside its glyph, the video element keeps native controls, and the ladder re-runs cleanly (button re-enabled in finally) as the retry path.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Driver run: rung-1 stop rendered as text; button re-enabled after run

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Do not fetch large media until it can actually be used; avoid duplicating identical heavy assets across routes.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The 117 KB asset is fetched only after the rung-1 probe passes, and the v153 page reuses the v152 copy by absolute URL instead of shipping a duplicate.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Driver run: no asset request on the blocked path (network log clean); curl of the shared URL returned 200 video/mp4 117384

summary: v153 refile of the v152 player at the feature's shipping-stage milestone. Two deliberate changes: milestone framing now says 'anticipated to ship in 153, still Proposed as of 2026-08-16', and the 117 KB Chromium test asset is referenced from the v152 folder by absolute URL (noted on the page) instead of duplicated. Verified via CDP-driven headless Chromium 141: honest rung-1 stop, no fetch on the blocked path, shared asset serves 200, clean console/network.
